definition: A space entirely devoid of matter.
example: The pump created a vacuum inside the chamber.

definition: Of uncertain, indefinite, or unclear character or meaning.
example: He gave only a vague answer to the question.

definition: The quality of being logically or factually sound; soundness or cogency.
example: The validity of the results was questioned.

definition: Disappear suddenly and completely.
example: The magician made the rabbit vanish.

definition: An element, feature, or factor that is liable to vary or change.
example: There are too many variables to make a prediction.

definition: Involving or including many different types or elements.
example: The restaurant offers a varied menu.

definition: Any of the tubes forming part of the blood circulation system of the body, carrying in most cases oxygen-depleted blood toward the heart.
example: The nurse found a vein for the injection.

definition: A risky or daring journey or undertaking.
example: They embarked on a new business venture.

definition: Relating to or in the form of words.
example: They had a verbal agreement.

definition: A decision on a disputed issue in a civil or criminal case or an inquest.
example: The jury returned a verdict of not guilty.

definition: Make sure or demonstrate that something is true, accurate, or justified.
example: We need to verify your identity before processing the request.

definition: Writing arranged with a metrical rhythm, typically having a rhyme.
example: She wrote a short verse for the occasion.

definition: Against (especially in sports and legal use).

definition: A ship or large boat.
example: The vessel sailed across the ocean.

definition: A person who has had long experience in a particular field.
example: He is a veteran journalist with 30 years of experience.

definition: Capable of working successfully; feasible.
example: They discussed a viable plan to reduce costs.

definition: Full of energy and enthusiasm.
example: The city has a vibrant nightlife.

definition: Immoral or wicked behavior.
example: Gambling was considered a vice.

definition: Deliberately cruel or violent.
example: The dog gave a vicious bite.

definition: Break or fail to comply with a rule or formal agreement.
example: They violated the terms of the contract.

definition: The action of violating someone or something.
example: The company was fined for environmental violations.

definition: Behavior showing high moral standards.
example: Patience is a great virtue.

definition: Expressing opinions or feelings freely or loudly.
example: She was a vocal critic of the policy.

definition: Solemnly promise to do a specified thing.
example: They vowed to support each other forever.

definition: The quality or state of being exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed.
example: They assessed the system for security vulnerabilities.

definition: Susceptible to physical or emotional attack or harm.
example: Children are vulnerable to certain diseases.
